title: MyRecon vs LeakCheck: OSINT & Credential Tools Compared
description: Compare MyRecon and LeakCheck: search inputs, credential exposure and verification limits. Choose an OSINT tool for authorized research.
h1: MyRecon vs LeakCheck: compare credential and breach workflows
intro: Compare LeakCheck and MyRecon by the question you need to answer. LeakCheck describes breach-record searches; MyRecon helps review public username candidates and supported exposure checks. This comparison does not establish superior accuracy or complete coverage.

sections.heading: What LeakCheck documents
sections.body: LeakCheck advertises breach searches with inputs including email and username, plus monitoring and API access. Its FAQ says access to compromised fields depends on the plan. This comparison does not reproduce exposure records or test paid capabilities.

sections.heading: What MyRecon checks and what a result means
sections.body: MyRecon checks public usernames across a supported catalogue of 500+ platforms. The chosen scan scope determines which checks run. Found means a lead for source review. Not found does not guarantee registration availability. Unknown means the check could not reach a reliable conclusion. Email and password-exposure tools are separate checks, not a complete inventory of every account.

sections.heading: Illustrative decision: Exposure response versus footprint cleanup
sections.body: For an exposure affecting your own address, review the affected account and secure reused credentials. For an old public biography, change its visibility or request account deletion. Removing a live profile does not erase historical copies; track both actions separately.

sections.heading: Access and costs before you choose
sections.body: MyRecon guest Quick scans show a limited preview. Standard scans require sign-in; account and plan limits apply. Paid features are described on the current pricing page. Check LeakCheck provider terms and available fields separately. This page does not claim either service is unlimited, always free or anonymous, and includes no paid-account or same-scope benchmark.

sections.heading: Record evidence and verify your next action
sections.body: For each authorized check, record the exact input, date, scope, result status and source URL. Keep unknown outcomes separate from negative results. Confirm accounts you own through an existing login or official recovery process, apply the privacy or security change, and recheck the specific exposure. A shared username alone does not identify a person.

faq.question: Is MyRecon a direct replacement for LeakCheck?
faq.answer: It depends on the task. Public profile discovery and breach-record searches have different inputs and evidence limits. Compare the required workflow before switching.

faq.question: Can I try MyRecon for free?
faq.answer: Guest Quick scans offer a limited preview. Standard scans require sign-in, and account and plan limits apply. See the current pricing page.

faq.question: Does a match prove ownership?
faq.answer: No. A shared username, similar name or historical record is not ownership proof. Keep uncertain matches unconfirmed and review independent evidence.
